sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Cell-surface expression confirmed by anti-Myc primary antibody staining (L2); no functional assay result (e.g., calcium flux, ligand binding) is reported in the cited clips — NOT MEASURED for function.
sites.rationale: P2RY1 is a GPCR with no annotated signal peptide; residues 1–55 form the extracellular N-terminal domain and TM1 begins at residue 56, placing the prepend site 55 residues from any TM boundary. The paper (L1/L2) explicitly states the double Myc tag is at the 'N-terminus extracellular region' of the full-length, membrane-anchored receptor, and surface display was confirmed by antibody staining (L2). Because no residue number is given and exactly one extracellular terminus exists, the position is topology-derived as a prepend (insert_after_residue=0). No signal peptide is present, so there is no cleavage risk. Full-length human P2Y1-R fused to a double Myc epitope tag at the N-terminus extracellular region, expressed in HEK293T cells (PMC9890698). The paper names no specific residue number; P2RY1 has no signal peptide (UniProt P47900), so the N-terminus (residue 1, Met) is directly extracellular and is the sole extracellular terminus of the receptor. The tag is therefore prepended before residue 1.

sources.claim: Human P2Y 1 -R (NCBI Reference Sequence: NM_002563.2 ) and P2Y 12 -R (NCBI Reference Sequence: NM_022788.3 ) were fused to double Myc epitope and rat AT1-R (NCBI Reference Sequence: NM_030985.4 ) to HA tag in N-terminus extracellular region.

literature_notes: Only two ledger lines are provided (L1, L2), both from the same publication (PMC9890698) and both describing the same construct: a double-Myc-tagged full-length P2Y1-R at the N-terminal extracellular region. No residue number is stated, but P2RY1 lacks a signal peptide, leaving exactly one extracellular terminus (the N-terminus, residue 1). The position is therefore topology-derived as a prepend. No ledger evidence supports any internal loop insertion (ECL1 110–126, ECL2 190–218, ECL3 280–305) or any C-terminal tag; those sites are not proposed. The paper notes that surface expression of P2Y1-R and AT1-R cannot be directly compared because they carry different tags (Myc vs. HA), but this does not undermine the surface-display result for P2Y1-R itself.
